links.outcome: Temporal performance drift of cardiac surgery mortality risk models on holdout 2017-2019 data
links.effect: Strong evidence of decrease in overall performance (CEM) across all models (P<.0001); all models decreased in at least 3 of 5 metrics; XGBoost CEM median fell by 0.0288 from 2017 to 2019.
links.quote: There was strong evidence of a decrease in overall performance across all models ( P <.0001).

links.outcome: Loss of accuracy relative to initial validation over time in temporally split holdout
links.effect: All models showed decreased CEM, AUC, and F1 over the 2017-2019 holdout; XGBoost AUC slope -0.000678; NN net benefit fell from 0.9035 to 0.8808 in projection.
links.quote: We found strong evidence that all models showed a decrease in at least 3 of the 5 individual metrics within the CEM.

links.outcome: Performance on temporally later external holdout versus development data
links.effect: Temporal external validation on 2017-2019 holdout showed performance decline across all models, demonstrating that earlier data overestimate later performance.
links.quote: There was strong evidence of a decrease in AUC performance across all models ( P <.0001).

links.outcome: Need for predefined thresholds for acceptable metric reductions triggering model updates
links.effect: Authors state metric-specific thresholds for acceptable performance reductions must be established before mandating updates; thresholds not determined in this study.
links.quote: Before mandating model updates, it is critical to establish metric-specific thresholds for acceptable reductions.

links.outcome: Comparison of ML models against EuroSCORE II on same data
links.effect: XGBoost CEM 0.728 and RF 0.727 vs EuroSCORE II 0.541; EuroSCORE II performed worst across all comparisons (CEM difference to XGBoost 0.1876).
links.quote: Furthermore, EuroSCORE II substantially underperformed against all ML models across all comparisons; this presents an urgent need to understand the drift effects of this score and is not limited to calibration drift.

unlisted_practices: variable importance drift (SHAP) monitoring to detect dataset drift
consensus composite metric (CEM) for ranking models over time
